header.act: ACT I — THE EASTERN FRONT BREAKS
player.speaker: Front Commissar
line.fekete-cold-open.speaker: András Fekete
line.fekete-cold-open.text: The station clock still says six; no one has had time to wind it. Trains from Zilah arrive without schedules—wounded men in cattle wagons, guns without teams, families asking whether Budapest is still ours. East of the sidings, Romanian artillery is already audible.
line.kun-field-wire.speaker: Béla Kun
line.kun-field-wire.role: People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs — Field Telephone
line.kun-field-wire.text: Böhm, every hour that railway remains open is an answer to Paris. Károlyi resigned rather than order the army behind another demarcation line; we inherited his empty depots and an ultimatum already marching west in Romanian boots. Do not tell me this retreat is merely a staff calculation.
line.bohm-opening.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
line.bohm-opening.text: That red pencil line is battalions without artillery and villages receiving three orders in one day. The Romanians crossed at dawn. We cannot stop them here; we can keep the railway open long enough to leave with an army.
line.bohm-political-objection.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
line.bohm-political-objection.role: Social Democrat and People's Commissar for Military Affairs
line.bohm-political-objection.text: Kun speaks of world revolution. The officers loading those trains speak of a country being cut apart, and most of the soldiers understand that language better. Build an army only from proclamations and it will dissolve when patriotism and socialism demand different roads.
line.kun-political.speaker: Béla Kun
line.kun-political.text: And build it only for the old frontiers, Böhm, and the officers will discard the councils the moment Paris offers them a flag without socialism. We need both motives today. Commissar, decide what Nagykároly buys us: time at the station, or freedom of movement on the roads.
Fortify the station and approaches. Every additional hour lets more men, guns, and rolling stock escape west.
Gain an entrenched infantry detachment and near-full core resupply, but forgo the prestige and reconnaissance experience of the mobile rear guard.
line.kun-political.choice.mobile-guard.t: Keep the rear guard mobile. Delay each enemy column, then withdraw before it closes the road behind us.
line.kun-political.choice.mobile-guard.h: Gain a prestige award and experience for every core reconnaissance unit, but forgo the infantry detachment and near-full resupply.
line.fekete-railway.speaker: András Fekete
line.fekete-railway.text: Then the station is the heart of the defence. I will keep locomotives under steam, send the wounded and artillery west first, and burn every timetable that can help the enemy. The infantry must keep cavalry away from the sidings until the last train clears.
line.bohm-mobile.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
line.bohm-mobile.text: A moving rear guard may save more formations, but each commander must know the road and the hour of withdrawal before the first shot. Do not let courage turn into a village-by-village last stand. Once the rails are cut, every gun becomes something the men must abandon.
line.bohm-final.speaker: Vilmos Böhm
line.bohm-final.text: Keep headquarters on the western road and the infantry between the cavalry and those trains. If we still answer the telephone at dusk, I can build an army from what reaches us.
